4:2.sourceText: κήρυξον τὸν λόγον, ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως, ἔλεγξον, ἐπιτίμησον, παρακάλεσον, ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ.
4:2.targetText: preach the word; be earnest in season, out of season; convict, rebuke, exhort, in all long-suffering and teaching,

4:3.sourceText: ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν,
4:3.targetText: for there will be a season when they will not endure the sound teaching, but they will heap up teachers according to their own desires—having an itching ear,

groups.note: Greek uses the definite article with the body-part/hearing phrase; LSV’s idiom having an itching ear uses indefinite an for that same auditory part, without a second invented Greek determiner.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

The reflexive recipient ἑαυτοῖς, for themselves, qualifies heaping up teachers; LSV omits a separate self-recipient. The actual earlier own adjective belongs to desires and is not exchanged with this reflexive.

4:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν, ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται.
4:4.targetText: and, indeed, they will turn away from hearing the truth, and they will be turned aside to the fables.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

review.note: Greek turns their hearing away from the truth; LSV turns away from hearing the truth, making hearing the English from-complement. The actual hearing and truth heads remain distinct with this attachment recast explicit; the second turning-aside predicate retains its passive form.

4:5.sourceText: σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν, κακοπάθησον, ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ, τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον.
4:5.targetText: But you—watch in all things; suffer evil; do the work of one proclaiming good news; make full assurance of your ministry,

groups.note: The evangelist/proclaimer noun εὐαγγελιστοῦ is rendered of one proclaiming good news; those English verbal/object pieces belong to that one actual designation, not extra original proclaiming verbs.

The actual πληροφορέω imperative can mean bring to fullness/fulfill; here it governs ministry. LSV chooses make full assurance, exposing the same underlying full-carrying-out head without converting the task context into an independent Greek assurance noun.

4:7.sourceText: τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα ἠγώνισμαι, τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα, τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα·
4:7.targetText: I have striven the good strife, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith;

4:8.sourceText: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος, ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ὁ δίκαιος κριτής, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ.
4:8.targetText: from now on there is laid up for me the garland of righteousness that the LORD—the Righteous Judge—will give to me in that day, and not only to me, but also to all those loving His appearing.

groups.note: The perfect active loving participle denotes those having loved His appearing; LSV gives loving without an explicit perfect auxiliary. The actual love predicate remains linked with that aspect wording difference explicit.

4:9.targetText: Be diligent to come to me quickly,

4:10.sourceText: Δημᾶς γάρ με ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν, Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν·
4:10.targetText: for Demas forsook me, having loved the present age, and went on to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia;

4:11.sourceText: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετ’ ἐμοῦ. Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ· ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν.
4:11.targetText: only Lucas is with me; having taken Mark, bring [him] with you, for he is profitable to me for ministry;

groups.note: The actual Mark object of having taken is also the understood object of bring; English repeats the same recruited companion as bracketed him. Both preserve the actual Mark identity without inventing another Greek pronoun.
The second-person reflexive σεαυτοῦ is rendered with you after bring, the same addressed Timothy accompanying Mark. The English construction does not require a separately repeated self element.

4:12.targetText: and I sent Tychicus to Ephesus;

4:13.sourceText: τὸν φελόνην, ὃν ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ, ἐρχόμενος φέρε, καὶ τὰ βιβλία, μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας.
4:13.targetText: coming, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus and the scrolls—especially the parchments.

4:14.sourceText: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο· ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
4:14.targetText: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil; may the LORD repay to him according to his works,

groups.note: Pinned N1904 ἀποδώσει is future will repay; LSV gives optative/wish may repay as TR ἀποδῴη. The actual repaying head remains linked with that mood difference explicit.

4:17.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με, ἵνα δι’ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος.
4:17.targetText: but the LORD stood by me, and strengthened me, that the preaching might be fully assured through me, and all the nations might hear, and I was freed out of the mouth of a lion,

groups.note: The passive πληροφορηθῇ here refers to bringing the preaching to fullness/accomplishment; LSV renders might be fully assured. This actual fulfill/fully-carry-out head is preserved with its task/preaching sense explicit, rather than teaching that the proclamation itself merely felt mentally certain.

4:18.sourceText: ῥύσεταί με ὁ Κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
4:18.targetText: and the LORD will free me from every evil work, and will save [me]—to His heavenly kingdom; to whom [is] the glory through the ages of the ages! Amen.

groups.note: The one actual me object of freeing is also the understood object of the coordinated saving predicate; English repeats it as bracketed me. Both English realizations retain the same written first-person object identity.
